networkHosts.artifact: Node headers and libs for a from-source native compile
networkHosts.observed: node-gyp's default dist URL, reached whenever the header cache is cold. NOW MEASURED, superseding the earlier note here that the fetch 'does not arise under nub': the isolated single-package macOS arm of 2026-07-31 caught `gyp http GET https://nodejs.org/download/release/v26.5.0/node-v26.5.0-headers.tar.gz` returning 200 during bigint-buffer@1.1.5's unconfined arm, on a harness that does set `npm_config_nodedir`. The cold-header fetch is real, not speculative. It is also not admitted by this entry in the case that matters: `fetchedBy` is matched against aube's INSTALLER-RESOLVED name, so a native-build dependency that shells `node-gyp rebuild` is spawned under ITS OWN name and gets nothing. Whether that class needs a blanket grant is still open — it did not block in that arm, because the confined side never reached node-gyp at all (the lazy-bin shim recursed first).

Named in Prisma's own firewall-allowlist documentation, and since MEASURED under the jail (macOS arm64, 2026-07-31). `@prisma/client` is on this list because the download does not only happen under `@prisma/engines`' identity: @prisma/client's postinstall re-execs the `prisma` CLI, whose bundled `@prisma/fetch-engine` downloads the engines itself whenever they are not already on disk — the ordinary cold-store case, because aube runs the two postinstalls CONCURRENTLY (measured: both START within 3ms) and the client's routinely reaches the check first. Traced with DEBUG=prisma:* inside the confined spawn: `prisma:fetch-engine:download https://binaries.prisma.sh/all_commits/<sha>/darwin-arm64/libquery_engine.dylib.node.gz will be downloaded to <store>/@prisma+engines@6.19.3/...`; without the grant the same request returns `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND binaries.prisma.sh`. npm on the identical fixture, with a cold npm cache AND a cold HOME, performs the same download from the same script — so this matches npm rather than widening past it.
Resolved by cypress's postinstall in the corpus harness-validation run. Paired with cdn.cypress.io because the 302 lands there; granting only one leaves the install broken.

Resolved by cypress's postinstall in the corpus harness-validation run, as the redirect target of download.cypress.io. cypress is the one corpus package that installs successfully under this four-host list.

packageNetwork.comment: Per-package egress that names no host. Identical grant to being listed in a networkHosts entry's fetchedBy, but WITHOUT adding a hostname to $downloads — which is also the allowlist for nub's own out-of-jail prefetch. Every entry below fetches a github.com release asset; github.com stays refused in notGranted for the prefetcher's sake, and these packages reach it because the review that added them here ratified them, which is the control the jail actually relies on.

full.observed: Isolated single-package macOS arm, 2026-07-31. Confined: `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND github.com` fetching https://github.com/railwayapp/cli/releases/download/v5.30.1/railway-v5.30.1-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz, no artifact. Unconfined, same fixture: DID-WORK-AND-SUCCEEDED.

Isolated single-package macOS arm, 2026-07-31. Confined: `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND github.com` fetching https://github.com/cube-js/cube.js/releases/download/v1.4.4/cubestored-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz, no artifact. Unconfined, same fixture: DID-WORK-AND-SUCCEEDED.

Isolated single-package macOS arm, 2026-07-31. Confined: `Hugo binary installation failed! Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND github.com`, postinstall exit 1. Unconfined, same fixture: `Hugo binary successfully installed!`, exit 0. The clearest control pair in the set — the package prints its own verdict either way.

Isolated single-package macOS arm, 2026-07-31. Confined: `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND github.com` fetching https://github.com/HandBrake/HandBrake/releases/download/1.11.1/HandBrakeCLI-1.11.1.dmg, no artifact. Unconfined, same fixture: DID-WORK-AND-SUCCEEDED with a 106065024 B HandbrakeCLI. WITH THIS GRANT the download is restored (38059875 B mac.dmg on disk, verified by size against the unconfined arm) and the package STILL FAILS, at `hdiutil attach mac.dmg` -> `hdiutil: attach failed - Device not configured`. Attaching a disk image needs diskarbitrationd, which Seatbelt refuses and no catalog field can grant. The entry is earned on the measured egress denial; do not read the remaining failure as needing a wider grant, and do not count this package as fixed.

Isolated single-package macOS arm, 2026-07-31. Confined: node-pre-gyp `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND github.com` on https://github.com/adnanrahic/node-gcstats/archive/refs/tags/1.5.9.tar.gz. STATED PLAINLY: this grant does NOT on its own make the package install. Verified with the grant applied — the request now REACHES github and returns `404 Not Found` on that URL, so the grant does exactly its job, but the tag is gone upstream and node-pre-gyp falls back to a source compile that dies on `aube: node-gyp shim re-entered 4 times without reaching a real node-gyp`. Two separate reasons, neither a wider grant: a dead upstream artifact (this package fails on plain npm too) and a nub defect.

packageGrants.mechanism: scripts/postinstall.js does four things, and each masks the next: it calls process.chdir(INIT_CWD); createDefaultGeneratedThrowFiles unconditionally mkdirs path.join(__dirname, '../../../.prisma'), a sibling of @prisma in the package's own enclosing node_modules; it looks for the prisma CLI; then it re-execs that CLI as `prisma generate`, which reads the consumer's prisma/ schema directory. The CLI lookup is why the dependencyDirs are here and not the schema: `require.resolve('prisma')` ALWAYS throws on 6.19.3 (its exports map points `.` at ./build/types.js, which the published tarball does not contain — reproduced on plain node with no sandbox), so the script always falls through to `exec('prisma -v')`, and the CLI it then runs writes the query engine into `@prisma/engines`' package directory and copies it into its own. Those two directories belong to OTHER packages, so package_dir does not cover them. The generated client itself lands inside package_dir and needs no grant.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM mkdir <own node_modules>/.prisma, then EPERM uv_cwd on chdir(INIT_CWD), then EPERM reading the consumer's prisma/ schema. The dependencyDirs were measured separately (macOS arm64, 2026-07-31) with a write probe run INSIDE the real confined spawn: writes to the `prisma` CLI cell and the `@prisma/engines` cell both returned EPERM while the package's own dir returned OK, and the resulting failure was `ENOENT copyfile <store>/prisma@6.19.3/node_modules/prisma/libquery_engine-darwin-arm64.dylib.node`. Verified by artifact, not exit code: 6 files carrying a per-run schema nonce, identical to the unconfined arm, against 0 without the grants — on a COLD store with no artificial delay. Presence alone is not a valid check here — the script writes throw-stubs before every guard, so it exits 0 having generated nothing; and neither is the absence of the `please install Prisma CLI` warning, which a warm store suppresses on its own.

packageGrants.mechanism: Its postinstall runs `indefinitely-typed`, which computes path.resolve(cwd, '../..'), asserts that directory is named node_modules, then mkdirs @types there and copySyncs each --folder argument into it. The write target is <own node_modules>/@types — the same enclosing-node_modules sibling shape as Prisma, under a different name.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM mkdir <own node_modules>/@types. With the grant, 20 copied type folders present; without it, absent.

packageGrants.mechanism: config/scripts/postinstall.js reads the CONSUMER's package.json for msw.workerDirectory, returns silently if absent, and otherwise re-execs its own CLI with cwd set to INIT_CWD to copy mockServiceWorker.js into each listed directory. The directories come from the field rather than a literal because msw imposes no convention — the consumer picks them.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM uv_cwd. The cwd need bites first: without projectCwd the child dies in uv_cwd before it reads the field at all. With the grants, msw's worker script is present; without them, absent.

notGranted.comment: Documentation only. Nothing in this object is compiled into any allowlist; it records hosts that a real install was measured to need and that were not admitted, so a contributor can see the bar before opening a PR. A build-time check keeps this list and networkHosts disjoint. Entries carry the same provenance fields as networkHosts, because an evidenced candidate is what makes a later promotion reviewable — `observedUrl` in particular is what a path-scoped grant would have to be written against.

hosts.requester: cube-js native installer (`Cube.js Native Installer`); 46 corpus packages total, 14 of them blocking
hosts.detail: The demand is real and measured, and the refusal is NOT about the download. github.com carries `git-receive-pack` — an authenticated write on the same hostname — and CI routinely hands lifecycle scripts a token with push rights, so a host-level grant opens a push path rather than only a fetch path. Host-level DNS gating cannot separate the two. A path-scoped grant limited to /*/*/releases/download/ would, which is the argument for building proxy path support rather than treating this host as permanently refused.
hosts.observed: FetchError: request to <url> failed, reason: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN github.com — the denied arm of the Linux corpus run.

hosts.requester: @tensorflow/tfjs-node, chromedriver (also puppeteer and taiko on the earlier macOS pass)
hosts.detail: Refused because an attacker can rent a bucket under the same hostname and read back whatever a confined script writes there — the exfiltration criterion, not an integrity one. The two observed prefixes (/tensorflow/ and /chrome-for-testing-public/) are stable and single-tenant, so this is a second candidate for a path-scoped grant.
hosts.observed: Both artifacts requested in the denied arm of the Linux corpus run; libtensorflow logged as `* Downloading libtensorflow` immediately before the URL.

hosts.detail: A soft fetch that degrades rather than failing does not earn an entry: the CLI reports `failed to install amplify binary` with egress denied, but the install itself still exits 0.
hosts.observed: Error fetching release: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN package.cli.amplify.aws, followed by `failed to install amplify binary`, in the denied arm of the Linux corpus run.

hosts.detail: Recorded as an evidenced candidate, not as a disqualification: no write-capable route or multi-tenant namespace has been established for it, and the fetch is a dedicated single-tenant vendor binary path. Whether it is admitted is a maintainer call, and it is deliberately left out of networkHosts until then. Note the requester is wrangler 1.x, which prints its own deprecation notice directing users to the `wrangler` package — so the demand may not survive the version it was measured on.
hosts.observed: Downloading release from <url>, then Error fetching release: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN workers.cloudflare.com, in the denied arm of the Linux corpus run.
